subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In Celtic folk music, a 'jig' is most commonly in which metre?
questions.explain: The jig is a lively dance typically in compound 6/8 time.

questions.q: In a major key, which chord built on the dominant typically functions as the dominant seventh?
options: A major seventh chord on the tonic
A minor seventh chord on the supertonic
A major-minor (dominant) seventh chord on scale degree 5
A diminished seventh chord on the leading note
questions.explain: The dominant seventh is a major-minor seventh chord built on the fifth degree, comprising a major triad plus a minor seventh.

questions.q: A 'cyclic' or 'ostinato' pattern, common in African drumming, is...?
options: A short rhythmic or melodic pattern repeated continuously as a foundation
A pattern that constantly changes and never repeats
questions.explain: Cyclic patterns repeat a short rhythmic or melodic cell continuously, forming the music's foundation.

questions.q: A recitative in Baroque opera primarily serves which function?
options: To advance the plot through speech-like singing
To display vocal virtuosity in an aria
questions.explain: Recitative uses a free, speech-like vocal style to carry the narrative between arias.

questions.q: A diminished seventh chord is built from which stacked intervals?
options: A major third and two minor thirds
questions.explain: The diminished seventh chord consists of three stacked minor thirds, dividing the octave symmetrically.

questions.q: When 'arranging' an existing melody for a new ensemble, a composer is chiefly concerned with...?
options: Transposing it down exactly one semitone only
Inventing an entirely new melody unrelated to the original
Re-scoring and adapting existing material for different forces while retaining its essence
questions.explain: Arranging adapts and re-scores existing material for different forces while preserving its identity.

questions.q: A ritornello in a Baroque concerto is which element?
options: A recurring orchestral refrain returning between solo episodes
questions.explain: Ritornello form alternates a recurring tutti theme (ritornello) with contrasting solo episodes.

questions.q: In African drumming traditions, the West African 'djembe' is...?
options: A set of tuned metal gongs
questions.explain: The djembe is a goblet-shaped West African hand drum capable of a wide range of tones.

questions.q: An Alberti bass is which kind of accompaniment figure?
options: A broken-chord pattern in the left hand of keyboard music
questions.explain: The Alberti bass breaks a chord into a steady low-high-middle-high arpeggiated pattern, common in the Classical era.

questions.q: In the typical structure of a North Indian raga performance, the opening section is the 'alap', which is characterised by...?
options: A slow, free, unmetred exploration of the raga without tabla
A fast, fixed composition with drumming
questions.explain: The alap is the slow, unmetred opening that introduces the raga's notes, performed without the tabla.

questions.q: The technique of word-painting describes which practice?
options: Music that reflects the literal meaning of the text
Painting visual scenery for an opera
questions.explain: Word-painting depicts the meaning of the words in the music, such as rising lines on the word 'ascend'.

questions.q: A Lied is which type of composition?
options: A German art song for voice and piano
questions.explain: The Lied is a German Romantic art song, typically for solo voice and piano.

questions.q: In sub-Saharan African music, 'polyrhythm' refers to...?
options: The use of only one drum
A gradual slowing of the pulse
The simultaneous combination of two or more contrasting rhythms
A single rhythm played in unison by all performers
questions.explain: Polyrhythm layers two or more contrasting rhythms sounding at once, a defining feature of much African music.

questions.q: The minuet and trio movement of a Classical symphony is typically in which metre?
questions.explain: The minuet, derived from a dance, is in a moderate triple metre.

questions.q: In music production, 'panning' controls...?
options: The placement of a sound within the stereo field (left to right)
The amount of reverb on a track
The overall loudness of the master
questions.explain: Panning positions a sound across the stereo image from left to right.

questions.q: A passing note is which type of non-chord tone?
options: A note that returns to its starting pitch
Approached by leap and left by step
Approached and left by step in the same direction filling a melodic gap
A sustained dissonance held over a barline
questions.explain: A passing note connects two chord tones a third apart, approached and quitted by step in the same direction.

questions.q: A secondary dominant such as V of V in C major would be which chord?
questions.explain: In C major, the dominant is G, and the dominant of G (V of V) is a D major chord.

questions.q: Which composer wrote the Brandenburg Concertos?
questions.explain: J. S. Bach composed the six Brandenburg Concertos, exemplars of the late Baroque concerto.

questions.q: The concerto grosso typically contrasts which two performing groups?
questions.explain: The Baroque concerto grosso opposes a small group of soloists (concertino) against the full ensemble (ripieno or tutti).

questions.q: Which woodwind instrument was a notable addition to the orchestra during the Classical-to-Romantic expansion?
questions.explain: The clarinet became a standard orchestral instrument from the late Classical period onward.

questions.q: 'Scat singing' in jazz is...?
options: Singing only the written lyrics with no variation
Singing in strict unison with the bass line
Vocal improvisation using nonsense syllables to imitate an instrument
questions.explain: Scat singing improvises wordless, nonsense syllables, treating the voice like an improvising instrument.

questions.q: A German augmented sixth chord contains which intervals above the bass?
options: Major third and augmented sixth only
Major third, perfect fifth and augmented sixth
Major third, augmented fourth and augmented sixth
questions.explain: The German sixth comprises a major third, perfect fifth and augmented sixth above the bass note.

questions.q: A pivot chord in modulation is best defined as which of the following?
options: A chord borrowed from the parallel major
A chromatic chord with no diatonic function
A chord common to both the old and new keys used to effect the change
The final chord of a phrase only
questions.explain: A pivot chord belongs diatonically to both keys, smoothing the transition during a modulation.

questions.q: A perfect cadence is formed by which progression?
questions.explain: A perfect (authentic) cadence moves from the dominant (V) to the tonic (I).

questions.q: In a Classical concerto first movement, the cadenza traditionally occurs at which point?
options: At the very opening before the orchestra plays
Near the end, over a tonic six-four before the final tutti
In the middle of the development only
questions.explain: The cadenza, a virtuosic solo passage, typically falls near the movement's end on a cadential six-four leading to the closing tutti.

questions.q: In jazz performance, 'swung' quavers are most accurately understood as pairs of quavers played roughly as...?
options: A triplet feel, long-short (approximately quarter-eighth of a triplet)
A short-long anticipation on every beat
questions.explain: Swung quavers approximate a triplet division, giving a long-short 'lilt' to each pair.

questions.q: The standard Classical string quartet comprises which instruments?
options: Violin, viola, cello and double bass
questions.explain: A string quartet is scored for two violins, one viola and one cello.

questions.q: Handel's 'Messiah' belongs to which genre?
questions.explain: 'Messiah' is an English oratorio, a large sacred work for soloists, chorus and orchestra without staging.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, the 'tala' refers to...?
options: The melodic ornamentation of the soloist
The cyclic rhythmic framework, a repeating cycle of beats
questions.explain: Tala is the rhythmic cycle, a repeating pattern of beats that organises the music in time.

questions.q: 'Call and response' is a texture common in African (and African-American) music in which...?
options: The music has no fixed pulse
All voices sing exactly the same line throughout
Two unrelated melodies are played simultaneously
A leader's phrase (call) is answered by a group (response)
questions.explain: In call and response a soloist's call is answered by the group's response, an antiphonal texture.
